prompt.context: Our client is a supplier to the microwavable popcorn industry. They supply popcorn makers (e.g. Act II, Orville Redenbacher's) with the grease-resistant paper used to package popcorn kernels in a variety of serving sizes. In this industry, the quality of the paper is determined by placing a bag of freshly microwaved popcorn on a napkin and measuring the amount of grease that seeps through the paper packaging and is absorbed by the napkin. The R&D department of our client recently developed a new type of paper that doubles the performance of the paper. A new type of coating is applied to the paper that virtually eliminates any seepage of grease in the napkin test.
prompt.question: Should our client introduce this new product into the market?

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall market size?
clarifying_info.a: Overall volume in the market is 100 million sheets of grease-resistant paper per year.

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive landscape in this market?
clarifying_info.a: There are 4 players who supply paper in this market. Our client holds the largest market share (50%), with the rest split evenly among 3 competitors. Market share for all players has been stable over the last decade.

clarifying_info.q: How did our client achieve the larger market share?
clarifying_info.a: They were the first mover into the market.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any difference between the paper supplied by our client and competitors?
clarifying_info.a: All players have been producing and supplying essentially the same type and quality of paper since microwavable popcorn was introduced.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a history of innovations in the grease-resistant paper market?
clarifying_info.a: All players have been producing and supplying essentially the same type and quality of paper since microwavable popcorn was introduced.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any threat of popcorn makers vertically integrating?
clarifying_info.a: Not really. Popcorn makers differentiate on brand and are not really interested in entering production of what is essentially a commodity product.

clarifying_info.q: Is there pricing pressure in this market?
clarifying_info.a: Prices have been relatively stable over the last decade, though recently there has been some increasing pressure as the retail price for microwavable popcorn has been dropping.

clarifying_info.q: Will popcorn makers be able to differentiate themselves by using the new paper? Will they derive a competitive advantage?
clarifying_info.a: Our client has not had direct conversations with the popcorn makers. Initial focus groups with end-customers (buyers of popcorn) found that the amount of grease seeping through paper is not a concern for buyers, and introducing the new paper will not necessarily sway consumer buying decisions.

clarifying_info.q: Will producing the new paper require a large capital investment?
clarifying_info.a: The cost of setting up the new production will be minimal.

clarifying_info.q: Will the new paper increase our client's raw material costs?
clarifying_info.a: It currently costs our client $0.10 to produce each sheet of paper. The chemicals in the coating of the new paper increase the cost of a sheet by 20% to $0.12.

clarifying_info.q: Will popcorn makers incur any additional costs to accommodate the new type of paper?
clarifying_info.a: They will not incur any extra costs in production/packaging. In fact, they will actually save money. The old paper required popcorn makers to glue two sheets together before packaging to achieve the desired grease resistance (adding $0.12 to total packaging costs). The new paper allows popcorn makers to eliminate this step. Old total packaging cost: 2 sheets × $0.20 + $0.12 glue = $0.52. New paper needs only 1 sheet plus $0.00 glue.

framework: Understand the supply chain: client supplies paper to popcorn makers who sell to end consumers
Assess end-customer demand: does the new paper create value consumers will pay for?
Analyze volume impact: how does switching from 2 sheets to 1 sheet affect client's unit volume?
Analyze cost impact: new paper costs $0.12/sheet vs. $0.10/sheet (20% increase)
Develop pricing strategy: find a price range that (1) maintains client profitability and (2) does not increase total packaging costs for popcorn makers
Assess competitive dynamics and first-mover advantage; consider patent protection
Identify go-to-market steps: pre-selling innovation to popcorn makers, sales/marketing

questions.prompt: Walk through the supply chain and identify who the key stakeholders are and what their interests are.
questions.guidance: Candidate should map: client (paper supplier) → popcorn makers (direct customers) → end consumers. Key insight: the new paper's performance improvement (grease resistance) is not valued by end consumers per the focus groups, so the value proposition must come from cost savings in the supply chain, not from demand creation at retail. Talking to popcorn makers (client's direct customers) is the critical first step before any launch decision.

questions.prompt: If our client introduces the new paper and maintains current market share, what happens to its unit volume?
questions.guidance: Old process: popcorn makers glue 2 sheets per package. New paper: only 1 sheet needed per package. Therefore, even with the same number of popcorn packages produced, our client sells only half as many sheets. Volume drops 50%. Current volume = 100M sheets × 50% share = 50M sheets. New volume at same market share = 25M sheets.

math.setup: Market total = 100M sheets/year. Client share = 50% = 50M sheets. New paper uses 1 sheet per package vs. 2 sheets previously, so packages served = 50M/2 = 25M packages. New volume = 25M sheets.
steps: Packages currently served by client = 50M ÷ 2 = 25M packages
New volume (1 sheet per package) = 25M sheets
math.answer: Client volume falls by 50% to 25M sheets if market share holds constant.

questions.prompt: What price should our client charge for the new paper to maintain its current profitability? What is the maximum price it can charge without increasing popcorn makers' total packaging costs?
questions.guidance: To maintain profitability at 50% lower volume, the client must roughly double revenue per sheet. Old revenue per sheet = $0.20. New cost per sheet = $0.12. Floor price (break-even on margin): at minimum the client needs to earn the same total margin. Old contribution per sheet (excluding fixed costs) = $0.20 - $0.10 = $0.10 margin × 50M sheets = $5M total margin. New: must earn $5M on 25M sheets, so need $0.20 margin per sheet, meaning price = $0.12 + $0.20 = $0.32 is the absolute floor to maintain total margin (simplified; acceptable answer is price ≥ $0.40 to match old revenue per package). The better framing: old total revenue per popcorn package from client = 2 × $0.20 = $0.40. New revenue per package = 1 × new price. To match old revenue per package, new price = $0.40. Ceiling: popcorn makers' old total packaging cost = $0.52 per package. With new paper, packaging cost = 1 × new price + $0.00 glue. To not increase their cost, new price ≤ $0.52. Therefore the pricing range is $0.40 to $0.52 per sheet.

math.setup: Old packaging cost per package for popcorn makers: 2 sheets × $0.20 + $0.12 glue = $0.52. New packaging cost: 1 sheet × P + $0.00 glue = P. Client old revenue per package = 2 × $0.20 = $0.40. Constraint 1 (client maintains revenue): P ≥ $0.40. Constraint 2 (popcorn maker not worse off): P ≤ $0.52.
steps: Old popcorn maker total packaging cost = 2 × $0.20 + $0.12 = $0.52
Old client revenue per popcorn package = 2 × $0.20 = $0.40
New paper: 1 sheet per package, so new client revenue per package = 1 × P
For client to maintain revenue per package: P ≥ $0.40
For popcorn maker to not pay more than before: P ≤ $0.52
At P = $0.52, popcorn maker saves $0.00 vs. before; at P = $0.40, popcorn maker saves $0.12 per package
math.answer: Price range: $0.40 to $0.52 per sheet. Setting price at $0.52 maintains current packaging costs for popcorn makers while maximizing client revenue per package. Prices below $0.52 share cost savings with popcorn makers and could be used to gain market share.

questions.prompt: How can our client use this innovation to potentially increase its market share?
questions.guidance: A superior answer recognizes: (1) the rationale for introduction is cost reduction for popcorn makers, not retail demand creation; (2) pricing below $0.52 but above $0.40 passes some savings to popcorn makers, creating an incentive to switch suppliers; (3) this could attract the other 50% of the market currently served by competitors; (4) client should patent the technology to prevent competitors from copying and to protect first-mover advantage; (5) client must pre-sell this innovation because popcorn makers may perceive a nominal price increase from $0.20 to (say) $0.45 without understanding the net savings from eliminating the gluing step.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional steps should our client take to successfully launch this new paper and capitalize on the opportunity?

categories.name: Customer engagement
ideas: Have direct conversations with popcorn makers before launch
Demonstrate total packaging cost savings clearly to procurement teams
Conduct pilot programs with key customers

categories.name: Competitive protection
ideas: File patents on the new coating technology immediately
Lock in long-term contracts with popcorn makers to lock out competitors

categories.name: Pricing and commercial strategy
ideas: Price in the $0.40–$0.52 range to balance profitability and customer incentive
Consider tiered pricing or volume discounts to attract switchers
Use cost savings story as the primary sales narrative, not grease performance

categories.name: Operations
ideas: Ramp up production capacity before launch
Ensure supply chain for new coating chemicals is secured
Qualify new paper in popcorn makers' production lines

categories.name: Risk mitigation
ideas: Assess competitor ability to replicate the coating technology
Manage transition carefully to avoid volume gap during switchover
Model downside scenario if adoption is slower than expected

recommendation: Our client should introduce the new paper, priced between $0.40 and $0.52 per sheet
The innovation does not create end-consumer demand, but it creates significant cost savings for popcorn makers by eliminating the two-sheet gluing step

A price of $0.52 maintains client revenue per popcorn package while leaving popcorn makers no worse off; a lower price passes savings to popcorn makers and can be used to gain market share from the 50% held by competitors
risks: Popcorn makers may resist what appears to be a nominal price increase ($0.20 → $0.40–$0.52) without fully understanding the net savings; pre-selling and education are critical
Competitors could develop a similar coating technology, eroding first-mover advantage if patents are not secured
Volume transition risk: if adoption is slow, client faces 50% volume decline before new price compensates
New coating chemicals increase unit cost to $0.12; if pricing negotiations compress below $0.40, margins are squeezed
next_steps: Immediately file for patent protection on the new coating technology
Initiate conversations with popcorn makers to validate interest and educate on total cost savings
Develop a phased pricing rollout strategy in the $0.40–$0.52 range
Build production capacity for new paper while managing transition from old paper
